description: DWSIM is an open-source chemical process simulator for steady-state and dynamic flowsheets, used by students, researchers and industry professionals. Its use is global, and it began in 2004 from Excel macros written by Daniel Wagner Oliveira de Medeiros and runs natively on Windows, Linux and macOS, and on Raspberry Pi. It offers industry-standard thermodynamic property packages (equations of state such as Peng-Robinson, PRSV2, Soave-Redlich-Kwong and Lee-Kesler-Plocker; electrolyte NRTL and extended UNIQUAC), unit operations including pipes with hydraulic and heat-transfer calculations, controllers, spreadsheet blocks and Python script operations, and switching between steady-state design mode and fully transient simulation. It is free and open source under the GNU GPL v3 and CAPE-OPEN compliant; its first open-source CAPE-OPEN implementation won the CO-LaN CAPE-OPEN 2012 Award. A patron-supported edition adds extra unit operations, property packages and plugins such as an OPC UA client. Caveats: some advanced features sit in the Patreon edition, and validation against plant data is the user's task. For simulation it models chemical and process plants, including dynamic responses to upsets, for process safety, energy and digital twin studies. Related catalogue records include ALOHA and the Tennessee Eastman process benchmark.
